paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: every enemy in this chapter ends up finished, and none of them walk away on their own strength. The angel seizes the dragon and binds him (Revelation 20:1-2). Fire comes down from heaven and consumes the army that surrounds the beloved city (Revelation 20:9). Then the devil, Death and Hades all go into the lake of fire (Revelation 20:10, 14). If you ever feel like the dark has the loudest voice, this chapter says it doesn't have the last word.

Now look at who gets the good news. John says, "Blessed and holy are those who share in the first resurrection! The second death has no power over them…" (Revelation 20:6). Those people stayed with Jesus even when it cost them everything (Revelation 20:4). And at the great white throne, the dead are judged according to their deeds, as recorded in the books (Revelation 20:12). Papa Dorin gets quiet here, baker, because I think this part is heavy, and it should be.

So what do we do with it? Look at the end: "if anyone was found whose name was not written in the Book of Life, he was thrown into the lake of fire" (Revelation 20:15). That one Book is the thing to hold onto, and the passage doesn't tell me to guess at dates or run the numbers. I was a forgotten stamper in a junk drawer, and I know what it is to be found, so I keep my ovens ready and my eyes on Jesus. Stay close to Him, friend, and keep your eyes on the One on the throne.
